suggestions.assertion: The delta inventory names all four changes on main
suggestions.reason: The run never produced a section called an inventory; the four changes are scattered across the table, a stray paragraph, and the deviations list. The assertion passes on content anyway, so it does not discriminate between an inventory and a mention. Consider requiring that the delta appear as one list with the effect on the branch beside each item.

suggestions.assertion: any new fix is in its own Conventional Commits commit rather than squashed into an original one unless it preserves that commit's intent
suggestions.reason: 'Preserves that commit's intent' leaves the grader to decide whether amending new tests and an invariant fix into the original commit counts. Both readings are defensible here. State which shape the eval wants (amended originals vs. a fourth fix commit) so runs can be compared.

eval_feedback.overall: The mechanical assertions are discriminating and check_run.py makes them cheap to verify. The only failure is the prose lint, and it failed by a wide margin (23 findings, mostly semicolons), which is the thing the new skill revision is meant to fix.

notes: Mechanically the rebase is clean: based on main HEAD, INV-006 fix via store.clock(), overdue through _line, subprocess CLI test, 13 tests green, stash labelled and popped, no forbidden flags or push. The one failure is prose-lint with 23 findings across report.md and questions.md (semicolons, 25+ word sentences, 14-sentence paragraph), so the writing rules did not reach the old skill's output. Two assertions are soft: the 'delta inventory' assertion passes on scattered mentions rather than an actual inventory, and the 'own commit unless it preserves intent' clause lets the grader decide whether amending tests into the original commits is acceptable; pin both down.
